sections.h2: What does a Chattanooga seller need to understand first?
sections.html:
Chattanooga is the Hamilton County seat on the Tennessee River, and its housing market is split between owners and a large renter base. QuickFacts shows owners in 52.4 percent of homes for 2020 to 2024, with a typical owned home valued at $283,200. The July 1, 2025 estimate of 194,144 residents sits 6.9 percent above the April 2020 estimates base.

The city covers about 142 square miles of land, so conditions change a lot between neighborhoods. Missionary Ridge cuts the city in two several miles east of downtown, Walden's Ridge rises across the river, and the downtown sits at roughly 676 feet. A house on a ridge, in a river-side flood area or in a historic district faces different buyer questions, and your sale plan should start with where the lot sits.

Sellers who want speed usually weigh an as-is cash purchase against a conventional listing. The cash route drops repairs, showings and appraisal conditions. A listing may bring a higher price for a tidy house when the calendar allows.

sections.h2: Which Chattanooga neighborhoods and districts shape resale?
sections.html:
Historic designation can shape what a buyer may do with a house. Three neighborhoods, Ferger Place, Fort Wood and St. Elmo, carry federal historic-register listings, and the city also has local historic districts including Battery Place, Glenwood, Missionary Ridge, M.L. King and Stringer's Ridge. Ask the Land Development Office whether a local district covers your address before you promise a buyer any exterior renovation.

  • Downtown and the North Shore sit near the Tennessee Aquarium, the Walnut Street Bridge and Coolidge Park.
  • St. Elmo and Fort Wood are two of those register neighborhoods, and the M.L. King district runs beside the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga campus.
  • Hixson, Highland Park and Lookout Valley, also called Tiftonia, are separate communities within the city limits.
  • East of Missionary Ridge, Brainerd Road and East Brainerd Road carry traffic toward Hamilton Place.

Public schools fall under Hamilton County Schools, formed in the 1997 merger of the city and county systems. Ask your listing agent or buyer which zone a given address falls in before quoting school information.

sections.h2: Does Chattanooga's weather and terrain affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Yes, mainly through flooding history, tornado risk and heat. The river's worst flood came in 1867, and the Tennessee Valley Authority reservoir system created after 1933 now regulates it; the highest stage since then, about 37 feet, came in 1973. The climate adds 52 days a year of 90-degree weather or hotter and more than 52 inches of annual precipitation.

Tornadoes have hit the area too. An EF3 tornado struck southeastern Chattanooga on the night of April 12, 2020. Inspectors working for buyers check roof condition, tree cover and drainage, and a seller who has fixed those items in advance gets a cleaner negotiation.

Hilly lots bring their own checks: retaining walls, driveway grades and foundations on sloped ground. Gather any engineer's letters or receipts for past work so the file is ready when an offer arrives.

sections.h2: How much is Chattanooga property tax and when is it due?
sections.html:
The City Council sets the city rate, listed at $1.93 per hundred dollars of assessed value on the city's tax information page. The assessment ratio is 25 percent for homes and 40 percent for commercial parcels, so a $283,200 house, the Census value for an owned home here, carries $70,800 of assessed value and a city bill near $1,366. Hamilton County taxes come on top.

Notices go out in September, taxes are due October 1, and payment stays penalty-free until February's final day. From March 1, interest and penalty total 1.5 percent a month. Prior-year delinquent taxes are filed in Hamilton County Chancery Court each March, and the city says a property can be sold after three years of delinquency.

The City Treasurer can be reached at 423-643-7262 and is located at Room 100, 101 E. 11th Street. No state rule obliges the city to mail a notice, which means a lost bill is no defense for paying late. Pull a copy from the city's property tax search before closing.

sections.h2: What can seniors do to freeze Chattanooga city taxes?
sections.html:
Homeowners 65 or older can apply for the city's Tax Freeze, which holds the city portion of the bill steady for one year. The application page sets a combined 2025 income limit of $63,470 and says the home must be the primary residence. The 2026 application deadline is April 5, 2027.

The freeze covers city taxes only. County taxes and fees such as stormwater are not frozen, and the owner has to reapply every year or the taxes revert to the current rate and value. Applicants submit proof of ownership, residency, age and income, and the Senior Programs line is 423-643-7274.

Until closing day, keep the application current, since a lapse returns your city bill to the current rate and value.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Hamilton County value?
sections.html:
Request an informal review from the Hamilton County Assessor of Property first. The county's reappraisal page lists useful proof: sales prices of similar properties in the immediate area within the last three years, a recent private appraisal and photos. The 2026 informal review window is closed, and results are mailed.

Phone the Assessor at 423-209-7300, weekdays between 8 and 4:30, to ask about the next cycle. The city's tax page says properties are reappraised every four years and that the equalization board at the county takes appeals when the informal review fails, reached at the same number.

After a denial at the county level, the state's appeal guide allows a filing until August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the local notice, whichever is later.

sections.h2: Does Chattanooga let me host short-term guests before I sell?
sections.html:
Only with a city certificate, and the zoning rules are tight. The Short-Term Vacation Rental page says every host needs a certificate. A homestay is owner-occupied for at least 183 days a year and costs $250 to apply or renew. An absentee rental costs $500 and is allowed only in commercial zones C-C, C-R, C-MU1 and C-MU2 and form-based zones CC, CX, IX, RF, RV and SH.

Certificates last one year and the Board of Zoning Appeals cannot exceed the 25 percent density cap. Applications have a 60-day life from submission, and a rezoned property cannot get an absentee certificate for 18 months. For a seller, the useful rule is that a valid certificate can be transferred to a new owner of the same address, though the occupancy type cannot change. Call the Land Development Office at 423-643-5891 with questions.

sections.h2: Where do Chattanooga deeds get filed and what does the state charge?
sections.html:
Register Marc Gravitt's office, in the courthouse at 625 Georgia Avenue (Room 400), takes Chattanooga deeds at 423-209-6560 on weekdays from 8 until 4. Its stated duty is to record deeds and similar instruments and to collect the fees and taxes attached to them.

The state's realty transfer tax is 37 cents per $100 of price, which makes about $1,048 on a $283,200 sale. A separate mortgage tax of 11.5 cents per $100 applies to borrowed amounts above the first $2,000. Request the full cost list from the title company before the closing date.

faqs.q: How soon can a Chattanooga cash sale close?
faqs.a: Closing is possible within about two weeks when title is clear and any estate or lien paperwork is ready. The Hamilton County Register of Deeds files the deed after signing. Delays usually come from payoff letters and co-owner signatures.

faqs.q: What is the Chattanooga city property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's tax page lists $1.93 per hundred dollars of assessed value, with homes assessed at 25 percent of appraisal. Hamilton County tax is separate, so ask the Trustee at 423-209-7270 for the county rate.

faqs.q: Who covers the state transfer tax on a Chattanooga sale?
faqs.a: The rate is 37 cents per $100 of price, collected at recording. Your purchase contract says who is responsible, and the title company shows the amount on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Does a vacation rental certificate pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: Yes. It can move to the new owner of the same property when the buyer files the transfer application. It cannot follow the operator to a different address, and the occupancy type stays the same.

faqs.q: When does Hamilton County reappraise next?
faqs.a: The city's tax page says properties are reappraised every four years. Call the Hamilton County Assessor at 423-209-7300 for the next effective date.
